messages:
jordan: Quick q about the embeddings endpoint behavior before I finish the SDK docs — want to confirm exact contract for inputs and truncation. Specifically: accepted types (str vs bytes), per-item truncation rule, per-request batch limits, and the return vector shape. Posting the curl I'm using below.

jordan: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1","inputs":["short text","<very long doc>...","你好"]}'

alex: tl;dr: accepts strings (utf-8) and arrays of strings only. We normalize to NFC. No raw binary payloads.

alex: Per-item truncation: we truncate by UTF-8 byte length to 32_768 bytes (approx 32KB). If NFC normalization changes length, truncation happens after normalization.

alex: Per-request limits: max 2048 items in the inputs array. We also enforce a soft cumulative byte cap of 1_048_576 bytes (1MB) for the normalized inputs; requests over that return 413 with a helpful message.

rina: @alex question — what's the behavior if an item is truncated mid-codepoint or mid-emoji? Any guarantee about not splitting surrogate pairs?

alex: We ensure we only cut at codepoint boundaries. We never split surrogate pairs or combining sequences; truncation will back up to the last safe boundary. If backing up causes the item to be empty (rare), we return the embedding for the empty string.

sam: Output shape for redwood-embed-1 is 1536 floats per input. Response format is: 
```json
{
  "data": [
    {"input_index":0, "embedding":[0.00123, -0.4321, ... 1536 numbers ]},
    {"input_index":1, "embedding":[ ... ]}
  ],
  "model":"redwood-embed-1"
}
```

sam: Note: we include input_index for stable mapping to inputs even if there are gaps. We do not reorder items.

jordan: Good to know we normalize and back up on codepoints. How do we handle empty / whitespace-only strings?

alex: Empty string -> deterministic vector equal to model's empty embedding (not null). Whitespace-only strings are first trimmed? No — we preserve whitespace (users expect different embeddings for "" vs " \n"). So we do NOT trim.

rina: backward compat: if a client previously relied on a smaller max batch, will requests that exceed the old limit but under 2048 get through? Is there any versioning header to opt into new limits?

alex: We bumped the soft limits last quarter. For compatibility we honor a header `X-Embed-Legacy-Limit: true` which applies the old limit of 512 items and a 256KB cumulative cap. Default is new limits. We documented this in the changelog and the SDKs set the header only when the user opts in.

jordan: Perfect. One more: if a single input after normalization is >32KB, we truncate and include a warning in the response per-item? Or do we return a top-level warning?

alex: We add per-item metadata when truncation happened: `truncated:true` and `truncated_to_bytes:N`. Example:
```json
{"data":[{"input_index":2,"embedding":[...],"truncated":true,"truncated_to_bytes":32768}]}
```

sam: Also FYI — embeddings are L2-normalized only in the client helper (SDK), server returns raw floats. We added a flag `normalized:true` in returned metadata only if we pre-normalize (currently false).

infra-bot: deploy-notice: embeddings-worker v5.2 rolled out to us-east-1 at 2068371700, handles new 32KB truncation + 1MB request cap. :package:

jordan: thanks all — I'll update the SDK docs and add examples for the legacy header + showing truncated metadata.

rina: quick follow-up later: can we add a small console lint that warns users if their batch is close to the 1MB soft cap? low priority but helpful.

alex: good idea — filing a tiny ticket and cc'ing eng-tools.

jordan: assigning docs PR to @sam and linking to the ticket. :thumbsup:
